typical_inputs: document corpus such as PDFs, markdown files, webpages, or support articles
evaluation questions with expected source documents
setup_commands: touch data/eval_questions.json src/ingest.py src/retriever.py src/evaluator.py README.md
pip install sentence-transformers faiss-cpu pydantic pytest
first_milestone_check: Running the retriever on one test question returns ranked chunks with source document IDs.
validation_checks: At least five evaluation questions have expected source documents.
Top-k retrieval returns at least one relevant chunk for a known query.
Generated answers cite retrieved sources instead of unsupported text.
common_errors: Chunk size is too large and returns full documents instead of focused passages.
Chunks lose source metadata during ingestion.
Evaluation questions are too similar to the indexed document titles.
The answer generator is evaluated without checking retrieval quality first.
typical_portfolio_artifacts: README section explaining chunk size and embedding choices
retrieval examples with cited source IDs
validation table with retrieval and citation results
interview_talking_points: Explain why you selected your chunk size and overlap.
Explain the difference between retrieval relevance and answer faithfulness.
Explain how your evaluation set tests failure cases.
Explain how citations reduce hallucination risk.
demo_strategy: Run one query and show retrieved chunks, source IDs, final answer, and citation coverage side by side.
deployment_path: FastAPI endpoint or Streamlit interface with query input, retrieved chunks, answer, and evaluation summary.
test_strategy: Use pytest with known questions and expected source IDs. Assert at least one expected source appears in the top 3 retrieved chunks.
